segments.text: A green Buy button, or an orange one? Which makes more people buy?
segments.caption: A green Buy button, or an orange one? Which makes more people buy?

segments.text: Don't guess. Test it. That's A-B testing.
segments.caption: Don't guess. Test it. That's A/B testing.

segments.text: Here's the definition, in simple words.
segments.caption: Here's the definition, in simple words.

segments.text: A-B testing shows two versions to two random groups of users,
segments.caption: A/B testing shows two versions to two random groups of users,

segments.text: then uses a hypothesis test to decide if the difference is real.
segments.caption: then uses a hypothesis test to decide if the difference is real.

segments.text: Say we split ten thousand visitors at random.
segments.caption: Say we split 10,000 visitors at random.

segments.text: Five thousand see the green button, and five thousand see the orange one.
segments.caption: 5,000 see the green button, and 5,000 see the orange one.

segments.text: Random matters: the groups are alike in every other way, so only the button differs.
segments.caption: Random matters: the groups are alike in every other way, so only the button differs.

segments.text: After a week, green gets four hundred purchases: eight percent.
segments.caption: After a week, green gets 400 purchases: 8%.

segments.text: Orange gets four hundred and sixty: nine point two percent.
segments.caption: Orange gets 460: 9.2%.

segments.text: Orange looks better. But is it real, or just luck?
segments.caption: Orange looks better. But is it real, or just luck?

segments.text: The null hypothesis: both buttons convert the same.
segments.caption: The null hypothesis: both buttons convert the same.

segments.text: If that were true, a gap this big would happen only about three percent of the time.
segments.caption: If that were true, a gap this big would happen only about 3% of the time.

segments.text: So the p-value is zero point zero three.
segments.caption: So the p-value is 0.03.

segments.text: Zero point zero three is below zero point zero five, so we reject the null.
segments.caption: 0.03 is below 0.05, so we reject the null.

segments.text: Orange wins: a fifteen percent lift in purchases. Ship it!
segments.caption: Orange wins: a 15% lift in purchases. Ship it!

segments.text: Watch out for three classic mistakes.
segments.caption: Watch out for three classic mistakes.

segments.text: Stopping the test early, the moment it looks good. Peeking like that raises false alarms.
segments.caption: Stopping the test early, the moment it looks good. Peeking like that raises false alarms.

segments.text: Skipping the plan for how many users you need. And changing many things at once.
segments.caption: Skipping the plan for how many users you need. And changing many things at once.

segments.text: So remember: split users at random, show two versions, and let a hypothesis test decide.
segments.caption: So remember: split users at random, show two versions, and let a hypothesis test decide.

segments.text: Plan the sample size first, and don't peek.

segments.text: Version B beats A by just zero point one points, with a p-value of zero point four.
segments.caption: Version B beats A by just 0.1 points, with a p-value of 0.4.

segments.text: What should you do?

segments.text: Not yet!
segments.caption: Not yet!

segments.text: Zero point four is far above zero point zero five. A gap like that is easily luck, so there's no winner yet.
